content: This medication, commonly known under brand names such as Pepto-Bismol and Pink Bismuth, is primarily used to treat occasional upset stomach, heartburn, and nausea. It is also effective in managing diarrhea and preventing travelers' diarrhea. The mechanism of action involves slowing the growth of bacteria that may be causing diarrhea. However, it should not be used for self-treatment of diarrhea if you also have a fever or blood/mucus in your stools, as these symptoms could indicate a more serious health condition. This medication is sometimes prescribed by a doctor in combination with other medications to treat stomach ulcers caused by the bacterium Helicobacter pylori. It is important not to use this medication to self-treat ulcers. The active ingredient, bismuth subsalicylate, is a type of salicylate. Always check the product label for ingredients, even if you have used the product before, as manufacturers may change the formulation. Additionally, products with similar names may contain different ingredients intended for different purposes. To use this medication, take it orally as needed, following the instructions on the product packaging or as directed by your doctor. The dosage depends on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. Do not increase your dose or take this medication more frequently than directed. Avoid exceeding the recommended dose for your age. If using chewable tablets, chew them thoroughly before swallowing. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or cup. This medication may interact with other drugs, such as tetracycline antibiotics or chloroquine, potentially reducing their absorption. If your doctor has instructed you to use this medication daily, take it regularly to maximize its benefits. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Side effects from this medication are rare. The most common side effects include darkening of the stools and/or tongue. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Persistent vomiting or diarrhea may lead to dehydration. Rarely, this drug can cause serious, potentially fatal bleeding in the stomach or intestines. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are also rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking bismuth subsalicylate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, aspirin, salicylates (e.g., salsalate), NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen, celecoxib), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Some formulations may contain aspartame. Since this drug contains a salicylate (an aspirin-like product), children and teenagers under 18 years old should not take it if they have chickenpox, flu, or any undiagnosed illness, or if they have recently received a vaccine. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. This medication may harm an unborn baby and cause complications with normal labor and delivery. It is not recommended for use during pregnancy from 20 weeks until delivery. If your doctor determines that you need this medication between 20 and 30 weeks of pregnancy, use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time. Do not use this medication after 30 weeks of pregnancy. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, but similar drugs do and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may increase the risk of bleeding when taken with other drugs that also increase bleeding risk. Carefully check all prescription and nonprescription medicine labels, as many contain pain relievers/fever reducers (NSAIDs such as aspirin, ibuprofen, or naproxen) that are similar to this drug and may increase your risk of side effects. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams a day), continue taking the aspirin unless your doctor advises otherwise. This medication may interfere with certain medical/lab tests (e.g., X-rays of the intestines using contrast dye), potentially causing false test results. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are taking this medication for diarrhea, drink plenty of water to reduce the risk of dehydration. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
